key_insight: Introduce Feature-space Smoothing (FS): a model-agnostic transform that smooths encoder latent features and yields provable, certified robustness guarantees for multimodal LLMs' feature representations.
problem_solved: MLLMs are vulnerable to adversarial perturbations that corrupt intermediate feature representations and cause wrong predictions; FS defends against such attacks by certifying stability in feature space.
method: Apply smoothing directly in the encoder's latent feature space (not the raw input) to produce a smoothed feature encoder that averages over small perturbations.
Derive theoretical certification bounds (a certified radius in feature space) that guarantee the smoothed encoder's output remains unchanged under bounded feature perturbations.
Make FS plug-and-play for existing MLLMs: wrap any feature encoder with the smoothing transform and optionally fine-tune to balance accuracy and robustness.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical, model-agnostic way to obtain provable robustness for multimodal models, improving reliability and safety for vision-language and other multimodal applications without redesigning architectures.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: original encoder -> Feature-space Smoothing block -> classifier, showing plug-and-play integration with MLLMs.
2D feature-space illustration: unsmoothed features showing decision flips vs. smoothed features with a certified robustness radius (circle) that preserves class labels.
Bar chart or table: clean accuracy vs. robust accuracy / certified radius comparison (baseline vs. FS-enhanced model).
Icon set: shield (robustness guarantee), gear (plug-and-play), theorem/checkmark (provable certification)
paper_title: Provable Robustness in Multimodal Large Language Models via Feature Space Smoothing
paper_authors: Song Xia, Meiwen Ding, Chenqi Kong, Wenhan Yang, Xudong Jiang
